# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to AI coding assistants (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, etc.) when working with code in this repository.


## Project Overview

**PowerUtils.BenchmarkDotnet.Reporter** is a .NET CLI tool (`pbreporter`) to help developers analyze Benchmarks in .NET projects. The tool was designed to work with reports generated by [BenchmarkDotNet](https://benchmarkdotnet.org/) and provides extract relevant performance metrics.

### Tech Stack

- **SDK**: .NET 10 (pinned in `global.json`)
- **System.CommandLine**: CLI parsing and command handling
- **Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection**: DI container
- **MarkdownLog**: markdown table rendering for the markdown exporter
- **Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub**: build-time source link support

### Key Facts

- It is a .NET CLI tool; the command name is `pbreporter` (`ToolCommandName` in the `.csproj`)
- This tool is designed to be run in CI/CD pipelines
- Distributed as a NuGet tool package (`PackAsTool`)
- **Entry point**: `src/Program.cs` - wires up DI and delegates to `ToolCommands`
- **Exit codes** (`src/Models/Constants.cs`): `0` = success, `2` = warnings generated, `3` = a threshold was hit

### Features

Actually, right now, it just has one command, but was designed to be extensible in the future.

#### Commands

##### `compare`

Compares two BenchmarkDotNet JSON reports between a baseline and a target, computing performance diffs and exporting them in various formats (console, markdown, JSON, hit-txt)


```bash
<tool> compare -b <baseline.json> -t <target.json>
```

**Options** (defined in `src/Options/`, wired up in `src/ToolCommands.cs`):

| Option | Alias | Required | Default | Description |
|--------|-------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `--baseline` | `-b` | Yes | — | Path to a file or folder with the baseline report(s) |
| `--target` | `-t` | Yes | — | Path to a file or folder with the target report(s) |
| `--threshold-mean` | `-tm` | No | — | Fail/flag when the mean diff exceeds this (e.g. `5%`, `10ms`, `10us`, `100ns`, `1s`) |
| `--threshold-allocation` | `-ta` | No | — | Fail/flag when the allocation diff exceeds this (e.g. `5%`, `10b`, `10kb`, `100mb`, `1gb`) |
| `--format` | `-f` | No | `console` | One or more of `console`, `markdown`, `json`, `hit-txt` |
| `--output` | `-o` | No | `./BenchmarkReporter` | Output directory for exported report files |
| `--fail-on-warnings` | `-fw` | No | `false` | Exit with a non-zero code when warnings are generated |
| `--fail-on-threshold-hit` | `-ft` | No | `false` | Exit with a non-zero code when any threshold is hit |

**Exporters** are registered as keyed transient services and resolved by the `--format` value:

| Format key | Exporter | Output |
|------------|----------|--------|
| `console` | `ConsoleExporter` | Prints a table to stdout; no file written |
| `markdown` | `MarkdownExporter` | `benchmark-comparison-report.md` |
| `json` | `JsonExporter` | `benchmark-comparison-report.json` |
| `hit-txt` | `HitTxtExporter` | `benchmark-comparison-hits.txt` (only when thresholds are hit) |

**Host-environment validation**: `src/Validations/ReportValidation.cs` compares the host environment of the baseline and target (OS, processor, core counts, etc.) and emits warnings when they differ, so diffs measured on mismatched hardware are flagged.

**Benchmark matching**: Reports are matched by `FullName` (namespace + type + method) using case-insensitive comparison via `Equivalente()`. Unmatched baselines are `Removed`; unmatched targets are `New`.


## Commands

### To build
```bash
# Build
dotnet build

# Pack the tool (Release only - packs to src/bin/)
dotnet pack src/PowerUtils.BenchmarkDotnet.Reporter.csproj --configuration Release
```
### To run
```bash
# Run the tool locally (from repo root after build)
dotnet run --project src -- <command> [options]

# Example: Compare two benchmark reports
dotnet run --project src -- compare -b <baseline.json> -t <target.json>
```

### To test
```bash
# Run all tests
dotnet test

# Run tests with coverage
dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"

# Run a single test class or method
dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~<TestClassName>"

# Run mutation tests
dotnet tool restore
dotnet restore
dotnet dotnet build --no-restore
dotnet stryker -tp tests/PowerUtils.BenchmarkDotnet.Reporter.Tests/PowerUtils.BenchmarkDotnet.Reporter.Tests.csproj -p PowerUtils.BenchmarkDotnet.Reporter.csproj --reporter json --reporter cleartext --reporter html -o

# Or
./stryker.bat
```


## Architecture

```
src/
  Program.cs            - DI registration and CLI entry point
  ToolCommands.cs       - System.CommandLine root; defines the `compare` subcommand and its options
  Commands/
    ComparerCommand.cs  - Core comparison logic: reads reports, matches by FullName, computes MetricComparison for each benchmark, applies thresholds, dispatches to exporters
  Models/
    FullJsonResport.cs  - Deserialized BenchmarkDotNet JSON schema (root)
    BenchmarkResport.cs - Deserialized single-benchmark entry (incl. host environment)
    ComparerReport.cs   - Output model: Warnings, Comparisons, HitThresholds
    MetricComparison.cs - Computes Diff/DiffPercentage/Status for a single metric
    ComparisonStatus.cs - Enum: Better | Worse | Equal | New | Removed
    TimeThreshold.cs    - Parses "-tm" values (e.g. "5%", "10ms")
    MemoryThreshold.cs  - Parses "-ta" values (e.g. "5%", "10kb")
    Constants.cs        - Project constants
  Exporters/
    IExporter.cs        - Generate(ComparerReport, outputDir)
    ConsoleExporter.cs  - Prints table to stdout; no file written
    MarkdownExporter.cs - Writes GitHub-flavoured markdown (benchmark-comparison-report.md)
    JsonExporter.cs     - Writes JSON diff report (benchmark-comparison-report.json)
    HitTxtExporter.cs   - Writes plain-text threshold violations (benchmark-comparison-hits.txt, only when thresholds are hit)
  Options/              - System.CommandLine Option subclasses (one per CLI flag)
  Validations/
    ReportValidation.cs - Compares baseline/target host environments and emits warnings on mismatch
    ValidationException.cs - Exception thrown for invalid input/reports
  Helpers/
    IOHelpers.cs        - ReadBenchmarkReports (supports file or folder, all JSON formats)
    BeautifyExtentions.cs - Formats ns/μs/ms/s and bytes for display
    ComparableExtensions.cs - Equivalente() for case-insensitive FullName matching
    PrintTable.cs       - TableBuilder used by the console exporter
tests/
  PowerUtils.BenchmarkDotnet.Reporter.Tests/ - Project with unit tests (mirrors src/ folder layout)
  test-data/          - Collection of JSON benchmark reports to use for tests
```

- **test-data** in `tests/test-data/` there are sample benchmark reports to use for testing. They are used in unit tests and validate the tool's behavior against known scenarios. In `docs/test-data.md` there are documentation and instructions explaining each test scenarios.The test data is versioned with the repository and should be updated when new test scenarios are added.

## CI/CD

GitHub Actions workflows live in `.github/workflows/`:

- `tests.yml` - restore, build, run unit tests and collect coverage on pull requests
- `sonarcloud-and-mutations.yml` - SonarCloud analysis and Stryker mutation testing
- `codeql-analysis.yml` - CodeQL security scanning
- `vulnerability-check.yml` - dependency vulnerability scanning
- `markdown-link-check.yml` - validates links in markdown files
- `publish.yml` / `release.yml` - pack and publish the NuGet tool and create releases


## Commit Message Convention

Commits are enforced by a git hook (auto-copied to `.git/hooks/` on build).

Follow the conventions in
- [@CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [@.agents/skills/git-commit/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/git-commit/SKILL.md)


## Code Style

Code formatting conventions are enforced by `.editorconfig` (UTF-8, 4-space indentation, CRLF, `final_newline`; 2-space indentation for JSON/YAML/XML).

### Source Code

- All the components should follow the **SOLID** principles and be designed for testability.
- Use Dependency Injection (DI) for all dependencies to allow for easy mocking in unit tests.

### Tests

- Use **xUnit** for unit tests.
- Use **NSubstitute** for mocking dependencies in unit tests.
- Use **Shouldly** for assertions in unit tests.
- Follow the AAA (Arrange-Act-Assert) pattern in unit tests.
- Use descriptive test method names that clearly indicate the scenario being tested and the expected outcome. Example `When_Json_Only_Contains_Two_Benchmark_Should_Return_Two_Record()`
- Use a CamelCase naming convention for test methods, starting with `When_*_Should_*` or `Given_*_Should_*` to describe the context, followed by the expected behavior.
- Use the `[Fact]` attribute for simple test cases and `[Theory]` with `[InlineData]` for parameterized tests.
- The class name of the test class should match the class being tested, with a `Tests` suffix. Example: `ComparerCommandTests` for testing `ComparerCommand`.


## Boundaries

- Each commit should be atomic and self-contained, with a clear purpose. Avoid mixing unrelated changes in a single commit.
- **NEVER** commit automatically without human review. **ALWAYS** ask for human review before committing changes.
- **NEVER** commit code that is not tested or does not have unit tests. All new features and bug fixes must include appropriate unit tests.
- **ALWAYS** run the unit tests tests locally before committing to ensure that all tests pass, doesn't introduce regressions and a good code coverage is maintained.
- **ALWAYS** run the mutation tests locally before committing to ensure that doesn't leave many surviving mutants.
- **NEVER** commit new tool feature without documentation. All new features must be documented in `AGENTS.md` and/or `docs/` and/or `README.md` as appropriate.
- **NEVER** commit sensitive information (passwords, API keys, secrets, etc.) in the code or documentation. Use environment variables or secure vaults for sensitive data.
- **NEVER** remove a failing test without fixing it. If a test is failing, investigate the cause and fix it before committing.
